title: Ela Goes Hiking
statementMd:
| ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bb77b99ba90b0cb682e230cf67edfd5352be2f57.png) | Ela likes to go hiking a lot. She loves nature and exploring the various creatures it offers. One day, she saw a strange type of ant, with a **cannibalistic** feature. More specifically, an ant would eat any ants that it sees which is smaller than it.*Curious about this feature from a new creature, Ela ain't furious. She conducts a long, non-dubious, sentimental experiment.* |
| --- | --- |

She puts $n$ cannibalistic ants in a line on a long wooden stick. Initially, the ants have the same weight of $1$. The distance between any two consecutive ants is the same. The distance between the first ant in the line to the left end and the last ant in the line to the right end is also the same as the distance between the ants. Each ant starts moving towards the left-end or the right-end randomly and equiprobably, at the same constant pace throughout the experiment. Two ants will crash if they are standing next to each other in the line and moving in opposite directions, and ants will change direction immediately when they reach the end of the stick. Ela can't determine the moving direction of each ant, but she understands very well their behavior when crashes happen.

- If a crash happens between two ants of different weights, the heavier one will eat the lighter one, and gain the weight of the lighter one. After that, the heavier and will continue walking in the same direction. In other words, if the heavier one has weight $x$ and walking to the right, the lighter one has weight $y$ and walking to the left ($x \gt y$), then after the crash, the lighter one will diminish, and the heavier one will have weight $x + y$ and continue walking to the right.
- If a crash happens between two ants with the same weight, the one walking to the left end of the stick will eat the one walking to the right, and then continue walking in the same direction. In other words, if one ant of weight $x$ walking to the left, crashes with another ant of weight $x$ walking to the right, the one walking to the right will disappear, and the one walking to the left will have to weight $2x$ and continue walking to the left.

Please, check the example in the "Note" section, which will demonstrate the ants' behavior as above.

We can prove that after a definite amount of time, there will be only one last ant standing. Initially, each ant can randomly and equiprobably move to the left or the right, which generates $2^n$ different cases of initial movements for the whole pack. For each position in the line, calculate the probability that the ant begins in that position and survives. Output it modulo $10^9 + 7$.

Formally, let $M = 10^9 + 7$. It can be shown that the answer can be expressed as an irreducible fraction $\frac{p}{q}$, where $p$ and $q$ are integers and $q \not \equiv 0 \pmod{M}$. Output the integer equal to $p \cdot q^{-1} \bmod M$. In other words, output such an integer $x$ that $0 \le x \lt M$ and $x \cdot q \equiv p \pmod{M}$.

## Input

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $t$ ($1 \le t \le 10^3$). The description of the test cases follows.

The only line of each test contains an integer $n$ ($1 \le n \le 10^6$) — the number of ants in the experiment.

It is guaranteed that the sum of $n$ in all tests will not exceed $10^6$.

## Output

For each test, print $n$ lines. $i$-th line contains a single number that denotes the survival probability of the $i$-th ant in the line modulo $10^9 + 7$.

## Note

Here is the example of $6$ ants moving on the branch. An ant's movement will be denoted by either a character $L$ or $R$. Initially, the pack of ants on the branch will move as $RLRRLR$. Here's how the behavior of the pack demonstrated:

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1d62449c2ee2e917bd72f5d639b2d6cf7940f5a8.png)

Initially, the ants are positioned as above.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/89a61ce356f1025932237b12faee51e46920db85.png)

After a while, the ant with index $2$ (walking to the left) will crash with the ant with index $1$ (walking to the right). The two ants have the same weight, therefore, ant $2$ will eat ant $1$ and gain its weight to $2$. The same thing happens with ant $5$ and ant $4$.

The ant $6$ will walk to the end of the stick, therefore changing its direction.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ea43548cd9fa4d90d6c43da96e89ce507bcf6fb2.png)

After that, the ant with index $5$ will crash with the ant with index $3$. Since ant $5$ is more heavy (weight=$2$) than ant $3$ (weight=$1$), ant $5$ will eat ant $3$ and gain its weight to $3$.

Ant $2$ will walk to the end of the stick, therefore changing its direction.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/96c4662a54e1e5498069b17ee0adeb1a80519dc7.png)

After that, the ant with index $5$ will crash with the ant with index $2$. Since ant $5$ is more heavy (weight=$3$) than ant $2$ (weight=$2$), ant $5$ will eat ant $2$ and gain its weight to $5$.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7add909f659381fdaa97f1d8218b218404560fab.png)

Lastly, after ant $5$ walk to the end of the branch and changes its direction, ant $5$ will eat ant $6$ and be the last ant standing.

<statement>
| ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bb77b99ba90b0cb682e230cf67edfd5352be2f57.png) | Ela 非常喜欢去远足。她热爱大自然，也喜欢探索大自然中各种各样的生物。一天，她发现了一种具有**同类相食**特征的奇怪蚂蚁。更具体地说，一只蚂蚁会吃掉它看到的任何比自己小的蚂蚁。*Ela 对这种新生物的特性感到好奇，但并没有生气。于是，她进行了一项漫长、可靠而又充满感情的实验。* |
| --- | --- |

她将 $n$ 只具有同类相食特征的蚂蚁排成一列，放在一根很长的木棍上。最初，所有蚂蚁的重量都为 $1$。任意两只相邻蚂蚁之间的距离相同。队列中第一只蚂蚁到木棍左端的距离，以及最后一只蚂蚁到木棍右端的距离，也都与相邻蚂蚁之间的距离相同。每只蚂蚁以相同的恒定速度，随机且等概率地朝左端或右端移动，并在整个实验过程中保持该速度。当两只相邻的蚂蚁朝相反方向移动时，它们会相撞；当蚂蚁到达木棍的一端时，会立即改变方向。Ela 无法确定每只蚂蚁的移动方向，但她非常了解蚂蚁在相撞时的行为。

- 如果两只重量不同的蚂蚁相撞，较重的蚂蚁会吃掉较轻的蚂蚁，并获得较轻蚂蚁的重量。之后，较重的蚂蚁会继续沿原方向行走。换句话说，如果一只重量为 $x$、向右行走的蚂蚁与一只重量为 $y$、向左行走的蚂蚁相撞（$x \gt y$），那么相撞后，较轻的蚂蚁会消失，较重的蚂蚁重量变为 $x + y$，并继续向右行走。
- 如果两只重量相同的蚂蚁相撞，朝木棍左端行走的蚂蚁会吃掉朝木棍右端行走的蚂蚁，然后继续沿原方向行走。换句话说，如果一只重量为 $x$、向左行走的蚂蚁与另一只重量为 $x$、向右行走的蚂蚁相撞，那么向右行走的蚂蚁会消失，向左行走的蚂蚁重量变为 $2x$，并继续向左行走。

请查看“说明”部分中的示例，其中将展示上述蚂蚁的行为。

可以证明，经过一段确定的时间后，只会剩下一只蚂蚁。最初，每只蚂蚁都可以随机且等概率地向左或向右移动，因此整个蚂蚁群共有 $2^n$ 种初始移动情况。对于队列中的每个位置，计算蚂蚁最初位于该位置且最终存活的概率。将答案对 $10^9 + 7$ 取模后输出。

形式化地，令 $M = 10^9 + 7$。可以证明，答案可以表示为最简分数 $\frac{p}{q}$，其中 $p$ 和 $q$ 为整数，且 $q \not \equiv 0 \pmod{M}$。输出等于 $p \cdot q^{-1} \bmod M$ 的整数。换句话说，输出一个满足 $0 \le x \lt M$ 且 $x \cdot q \equiv p \pmod{M}$ 的整数 $x$。

## 输入格式

每个测试包含多个测试用例。第一行包含测试用例数量 $t$（$1 \le t \le 10^3$）。接下来是各个测试用例的描述。

每个测试用例仅包含一行，其中有一个整数 $n$（$1 \le n \le 10^6$）——实验中的蚂蚁数量。

保证所有测试用例中的 $n$ 之和不超过 $10^6$。

## 输出格式

对于每个测试用例，输出 $n$ 行。第 $i$ 行包含一个数，表示队列中第 $i$ 只蚂蚁的存活概率，结果对 $10^9 + 7$ 取模。

## 说明

下面展示了 $6$ 只蚂蚁在木棍上移动的示例。蚂蚁的移动方向用字符 $L$ 或 $R$ 表示。开始时，木棍上的蚂蚁群按照 $RLRRLR$ 移动。以下是蚂蚁群行为的过程：

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1d62449c2ee2e917bd72f5d639b2d6cf7940f5a8.png)

最初，蚂蚁如图所示排列。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/89a61ce356f1025932237b12faee51e46920db85.png)

过了一段时间后，编号为 $2$ 的蚂蚁（向左行走）会与编号为 $1$ 的蚂蚁（向右行走）相撞。两只蚂蚁的重量相同，因此蚂蚁 $2$ 会吃掉蚂蚁 $1$，其重量增加到 $2$。蚂蚁 $5$ 和蚂蚁 $4$ 之间也会发生同样的事情。

蚂蚁 $6$ 会走到木棍末端，因此改变方向。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ea43548cd9fa4d90d6c43da96e89ce507bcf6fb2.png)

之后，蚂蚁 $5$ 会与蚂蚁 $3$ 相撞。由于蚂蚁 $5$ 更重（重量为 $2$），而蚂蚁 $3$ 的重量为 $1$，蚂蚁 $5$ 会吃掉蚂蚁 $3$，其重量增加到 $3$。

蚂蚁 $2$ 会走到木棍末端，因此改变方向。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/96c4662a54e1e5498069b17ee0adeb1a80519dc7.png)

之后，蚂蚁 $5$ 会与蚂蚁 $2$ 相撞。由于蚂蚁 $5$ 更重（重量为 $3$），而蚂蚁 $2$ 的重量为 $2$，蚂蚁 $5$ 会吃掉蚂蚁 $2$，其重量增加到 $5$。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7add909f659381fdaa97f1d8218b218404560fab.png)

最后，蚂蚁 $5$ 走到木棍末端并改变方向后，蚂蚁 $5$ 会吃掉蚂蚁 $6$，成为最后存活的蚂蚁。
</statement>
